title: Signal isolation and warmup tuning to mitigate autoscaler false scales
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: During a multi-tenant traffic spike on 2026-03-10 we observed repeated rapid scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs on the serving pool. This manifested as increased cold-start latency for customer requests and elevated error-rate during a 30 minute window. Investigation shows spurious KEDA trigger spikes from noisy external probes combined with too-short warmup and stabilization windows on the HPA leading to overshoot and oscillation.
impact: Approximately 12% of requests in the affected tenant slice experienced >=300ms cold-start penalty; two high-impact customers reported P1 latency regressions. Autoscaler churn increased GPU provisioning churn leading to higher cloud costs for the period.
timeline:
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Alerts for increased 99th p99 latency and instance spin-ups.
2026-03-10 09:18 UTC: First mitigation (temporary higher min replicas) applied by oncall.
2026-03-10 09:25-09:40 UTC: Flapping continues; oncall escalated to runtime lead.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Temporary routing fallback to lower-capacity pool to reduce customer impact.
2026-03-11 14:00 UTC: Root cause hypothesis validated in replay environment (probe spikes + short warmup).
root_cause: Two correlated issues: 1) Noisy scaling signal: an external monitoring probe pattern caused transient spikes that KEDA treated as legitimate demand; 2) HPA warmup/stabilization windows are too short for our cold-start profile, so by the time new replicas became ready, the signal had already fallen back, triggering a scale-down. There was also insufficient signal isolation per-tenant, so noisy tenants could affect shared scaling decisions in the blended autoscaler configuration.
investigation_notes: Replayed traffic from the incident window in a staging environment with KEDA metrics: reproduced rapid trigger bursts aligned to external probe timings.
Heap and kube-probe timings show new replicas reported ready before container image layers warmed caches, so RPC latencies remained high for first few requests.
Percentile-based metric smoothing (P95->P99) showed high variance in the trigger metric; current trigger uses raw counts without dampening.
Observed cross-tenant noise: a single noisy customer generated short high-frequency bursts that shifted the blended signal above threshold repeatedly.
Existing autoscaler logs lacked clear tenant tags for scale decisions; added tags for replay to correlate tenants with trigger spikes.
mitigations_taken: Oncall increased min replicas for the affected pool to provide headroom (temporary).
Routed traffic for top-2 impacted customers to a dedicated pool to reduce cross-tenant interference.
Disabled aggressive KEDA trigger source from third-party probe while we validated smoothing logic.
action_items: ENG-117254: Add percentile smoothing (rolling 90s P95->P99) and configurable dampening factor to KEDA scaler (owner: Marco Reyes; estimate: 3)
ENG-117255: Implement per-tenant signal isolation flags so KEDA aggregation can ignore opt-out noisy tenants (owner: Priya Singh; estimate: 5)
ENG-117256: Extend HPA warmup/stabilization window to include a 'post-ready warm period' to prevent immediate scale-downs until health and cache-warm checks pass (owner: Satoshi Ito; estimate: 3)
ENG-117257: Create a lightweight readiness probe extension that validates application cache priming (owner: Backend Team; estimate: 2)
ENG-117258: Add telemetry: tag scale decisions with tenant_id, trigger_source, and pre/post smoothing values; create dashboard with annotated incidents (owner: Observability; estimate: 2)
ENG-117259: Run 72-hour canary in staging with synthetic noisy tenant and validate no oscillation under configured thresholds (owner: Marco Reyes; estimate: 2)
metrics_observed: KEDA trigger count 99th percentile: +120% above baseline during spikes
Replica churn rate: 3x baseline during incident window
Customer p99 latency: increased from 85ms -> 420ms for affected slice
Error rate: transient 0.6% increase correlating with cold-starts
next_steps: Prioritize ENG-117254 and ENG-117256 into the next sprint; schedule pairing session between runtime and observability teams this week.
Ship smoothing change behind a feature flag and monitor for false negatives for 48 hours before enabling by default.
Coordinate with Customer Success to notify impacted customers of follow-up and mitigation timelines.
Document recommended probe cadence and add guidance to onboarding docs to reduce noisy external probe effects.
owner_notes: We will favor conservative dampening by default to avoid under-provisioning; any smoothing that delays necessary scale-ups must be validated against a synthetic cold-start workload. The plan includes a canary and rollback hooks. If smoothing introduces missed scale-ups for 2 consecutive business hours in canary, revert and iterate.
